title: Diabetes Insulin Self-Management Education (DIME) Web-based Application to Support People With Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) Starting Insulin in Hospital
official: Diabetes Insulin Self-Management Education (DIME) Web-based Application to Support People With Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) Starting Insulin in Hospital, a Mixed Methods Study.
summary:
The aim of this study is to find out the views of nurses and inpatients with type 2 diabetes of the Diabetes Insulin self-Management Education (DIME) web-based application. DIME was developed by nurses and people with type 2 diabetes, and a prototype was developed. The DIME app has been developed over a long period of time in response to the needs and concerns of people with type 2 diabetes starting insulin and a pilot study which led to the development of the original DIME programme. The current study involves introducing the DIME app to a small number of people starting insulin in hospital and the nurses who educate them and interviewing them about their thoughts on using it. The investigators will also count the number of people with type 2 diabetes who start insulin in hospital and the main reason for starting it over a 6 month period.

This project will help us to understand if a digital tool such as DIME might help to support in hospital insulin starts. The investigators will also know how many people are likely to need the support as they will have counted the number of people starting insulin when they have type 2 diabetes in hospital over a 6 month period. It will involve patients and nurses. The nurses involved will understand how, what, when, and why new technology such as the DIME app can fit within the hospital setting.

The study has been designed to address the following questions:

What are the views of people living with type 2 diabetes and nurses on the use of a web-based app to support in-hospital insulin starts? How many people with type 2 diabetes start insulin in hospital over a 6 month period and what is the reason for starting it?
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Patient Participants:

* Adults aged 18 and above.
* Adults with a type 2 diabetes diagnosis.
* Adults who started insulin as an inpatient
* Adults who understand and can communicate in English.
* Adults who have the capacity to consent.

Nurse Participants:

* Diabetes nurses working at King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
* Inpatient nurses caring for people with T2D

Exclusion Criteria:

* Adults who are not willing to participate.
* Adults with severe physical/mental illness or cognitive dysfunction/significant learning difficulties.
* Adults who are unable to speak or understand English.
